user.title: Which offer do you have?
user.description: Pick your offer if it is listed: its structure (known time ranges, weekends, special days…) will be pre-filled and you only need to copy the prices from your bill. Otherwise, choose “Other offer”.

contrat.title: Your contract
contrat.description: Supplier and offer name are free text, used for display.

data_description.prix_revente: Price at which injected surplus is bought back (EUR/kWh), as written in your resale contract. Leave empty if you do not sell your surplus.

prix_base.title: Price per kWh
prix_base.description: Price including tax, as shown on your bill. Weekend or summer prices (if your offer has them) are entered later.

plages.title: Peak and off-peak hours
plages.description:
Format 23:00-06:00. Several ranges: separate them with commas (e.g. 02:00-07:00, 13:00-16:00). Your off-peak hours are shown on your bill or in your Enedis account.

Optional: **super off-peak hours** (e.g. Charge'Heures, Octopus Go) and an **extra named period** (e.g. Modulo's “solar hours”). Leave empty if your offer has none.

data.perso_creuse: The extra period counts as off-peak

data_description.perso_creuse: Untick it if this period is more expensive (peak…).

calendrier.title: Weekends, bank holidays and options
calendrier.description: Tell what your offer provides. French bank holidays are calculated automatically.

data.jours_extra: Weekdays charged at the weekend rate (e.g. Zen Week-End Plus)
data.saisons: Different prices in winter and summer
data.jours_speciaux: Special days announced the day before (Sobriété, Jour Éclair, Jour Sérénité…)

data_description.jours_extra: These days follow the same rule as Saturday and Sunday.
data_description.jours_speciaux: Except Tempo, which has its own offer type.

weekend.title: Weekend price
weekend.description: Price charged at weekends (and on the chosen days).

data_description.prix_weekend_hc: Leave empty if the weekend price is the same all day.

ete.title: Summer season
ete.description: Tick the winter months; the others are summer. Prices entered in the previous steps are the winter ones.

jours_speciaux.title: Special days
jours_speciaux.description:
One or two kinds of days with special prices, announced by the supplier.

**How does the integration know a day is special?** The simplest way: a tap on the card, or the “Special day today / tomorrow” selects created by the integration (also usable in automations). If another integration already announces these days, pick its entity as the source: it will be followed automatically.

data_description.js_debut_h: 0 = midnight. Zen Flex: 8 (the day runs from 8:00 to 8:00).
data_description.js1_valeur: Default “on” (switch, binary sensor, calendar). For a text sensor, enter the expected value, e.g. Sobriété (case and accents ignored).

tempo.title: Tempo offer
tempo.description: A Tempo day runs from 6:00 to 6:00. Today's and tomorrow's colours and 15-day forecasts are fetched automatically (calendrier-tempo.fr, no account needed).

dynamique.title: Dynamic price
dynamique.description: The price changes every hour and comes from another entity (your supplier's integration, EPEX Spot, Nord Pool…). €/MWh and c€/kWh are converted automatically. If the entity publishes upcoming prices, they are used for forecasts.

data_description.dyn_majoration: If the source only gives the market price, add grid fees and taxes here in €/kWh to get the price you actually pay.

suivi.title: Consumption tracking (optional)
suivi.description: Pick the meter of energy **drawn from the grid** (Linky through TIC, Shelly EM, Enphase “lifetime net energy consumption”…) to get the cost of the day, week, month and year, and an estimate of your bills from your history. Leave empty to skip tracking.

data.mode_paiement: How do you pay for your electricity?

data_description.compteur: A meter that only increases. History already recorded by Home Assistant is used right away. Abnormal jumps (gateway restarting) are ignored.
data_description.puissance_compteur: Optional. Power drawn from the grid (W, positive when buying). One sensor, or three in three-phase (one per phase). Used to advise a subscribed power.
data_description.triphase: In three-phase, the subscribed power is shared between the three phases and the meter trips as soon as one phase exceeds its share.
data_description.depassements_toleres: A power exceeded during at most this many hours a year is suggested as possible with peak shaving or load shedding (10 by default).

paiement_mensualites.title: Monthly instalments
paiement_mensualites.description: You pay a fixed amount every month, then a balancing bill (usually once a year). Everything is optional.

data.date_debut_facturation: Date of your last balancing bill

data_description.mensualite_fournisseur: To find out whether it is too high or too low.
data_description.date_debut_facturation: To follow your balance since that date (refund or extra payment expected).

paiement_reel.title: Billed on actual consumption
paiement_reel.description: You receive a bill for your actual consumption at regular intervals, with no instalments.

data.date_debut_facturation: Date of one of your bills

data_description.date_debut_facturation: Used to align billing periods: any bill will do (the latest, for instance). The current bill, its estimated amount and the next bill date are derived from it.

error.plages_invalides: Unreadable time range. Expected format: 23:00-06:00, several ranges separated by commas.
error.mois_manquants: Tick at least one winter month.
error.nom_identique: Choose a name different from the first kind of day.
error.compteur_requis: Pick a meter: the instalment and balance are calculated from consumption.

date_effet.title: When do these prices apply?
date_effet.description:
**Price change**: your supplier announced new prices. Enter their effective date: the integration will switch on its own at midnight that day, and the old grid stays in the history. You can enter a change in advance.

**Correction**: you fix a typo in grid {grille}, without creating history.

data.date_effet: Effective date of the new prices

data_description.date_effet: Ignored for a correction. Default: today.

supprimer_version.title: Delete a grid
supprimer_version.description: The chosen grid is removed from the history. If it is the current one, the previous grid applies again.

puissance.title: Subscribed power
puissance.description:
Shown on your bill or contract (in kVA). It applies to the current grid and upcoming grids. Leave empty if you don't know it.

If your standing charge changes at the same time, use “Enter new prices” as a price change instead, to keep the history.

revente.title: Surplus resale
revente.description: Price at which your injected surplus is bought back (EUR/kWh). It applies to the current grid and upcoming grids; past grids keep theirs. Leave empty if you do not sell your surplus.

previsions.description: Returns upcoming price slots, the cheapest one, and the best slot for a given duration.

config_entry_id.name: Contract
config_entry_id.description: Contract to use (the first one by default).

duree.name: Slot duration
duree.description: If set, finds the cheapest continuous slot of this duration (in hours).

prix_passes.name: Past prices
prix_passes.description: Returns the prices of a past period, hour by hour, as the contract defines them today (corrections included).

config_entry_id.name: Contract
config_entry_id.description: Contract to use (the first one by default).

fin.name: End
fin.description: End of the period (at most 366 days after the start).

comparer_offres.name: Compare offers
comparer_offres.description: Returns what each offer entered would have cost over the given period (at most 366 days), standing charge included, with the real hourly consumption.

config_entry_id.name: Contract
config_entry_id.description: Contract to use (the first one if empty).
